their self-declared names without validating them against the requested
name. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause BCEL to return or
verify a different class than the one requested.

items.summary:

with extremely large frame sizes. An attacker could possibly use this issue
to cause dav1d to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or possibly
execute arbitrary code.

items.summary:

supplied by the caller, such as Authorization, Cookie and
Proxy-Authorization, when following cross-origin redirects, including
redirects from HTTPS to HTTP. An attacker could possibly use this issue to
obtain sensitive information.

incorrectly granted the whoopsie user unrestricted D-Bus access to
root-only methods. A local attacker who can execute code as the whoopsie
user could possibly use this issue to disrupt system networking or alter
NetworkManager logging and connection configurations.

items.summary:

identifiers during first-time SSH logins. A remote authenticated user could
possibly use this issue to access or modify files belonging to another
user, potentially leading to account takeover or privilege escalation.

items.title: USN-9197-1: Speex vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Speex incorrectly handled oversize input when
appending data to a bit buffer not owned by the library. An attacker
could possibly use this issue to cause Speex to crash, resulting in a
denial of service, or possibly execute arbitrary code.

items.summary: Led by the German Itzehoe Public Prosecutor's Office (Staatsanwaltschaft Itzehoe), the operation targeted a company suspected of supplying fraudulent trading websites to criminal groups. The entity is connected to call centre operators who allegedly persuaded victims to hand over their savings. items.title: Not a game: Europol and partners target terrorist role-playing online
items.summary: Europol’s European Union Internet Referral Unit (EU IRU) coordinated together with Spain a Referral Action Day targeting violent extremist and terrorist live action role-playing (LARPing) in online gaming environments. Specialised units from 16 countries participated in the action.

items.title: Five TEFAF robbery suspects added to EU Most Wanted
items.summary: As of 29 October 2026, five new fugitives, four men and one woman, have been added to the EU Most Wanted list. According to the Limburg Public Prosecutor's Office (Openbaar Ministerie) and the Dutch Police (Politie), all five suspects are involved in the European Fine Art Fair (TEFAF) robbery that took place on 28 June 2022 in Maastricht, the Netherlands.
